demographics.heading: What this means for you
body: These figures show who lives in Burton: how many residents, their ages, and how households are changing. They drive nearly everything the city plans for: how many homes and services are needed, where to focus senior or youth programs, and how much state revenue Burton receives (much of it is shared out per resident). A stable or growing population helps keep that funding steady.

jobs.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows where Burton residents work and who the area's largest employers are. A mix of stable employers and steady jobs means more people can work close to home, supports local businesses, and strengthens the tax base that pays for city services. It's a practical gauge of the local economy's health and resilience.

access.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows how affordable everyday life is in Burton: what households earn, and how much of that goes to housing and getting around. In an auto-dependent suburb, transportation can cost nearly as much as housing, so the combined burden matters more than rent or a mortgage alone. Where these numbers run high, families have less left over for everything else.

housing.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows Burton's housing: how many homes there are, what they're worth, and how much is being built or improved. It affects what you'd pay to buy or rent here, your own home's value, and the property-tax base that funds city services. Steady building permits and rising values signal a healthy market; very little new construction can mean tighter supply and higher prices.

zoning.heading: What this means for you
body: Zoning is the rulebook for what can be built where: homes, shops, offices, or industry. It shapes your neighborhood's character, what can open near you, and where the city expects to grow. If you're planning to build, add on, or open a business, your parcel's zoning is the first thing that decides what's allowed.

schools.heading: What this means for you
body: Burton is served by several school districts, and this shows how each is doing. Schools affect your children's education, your home's value, and a big share of your tax bill (see Property Taxes). Because the city spans 7 districts, the fair comparison is district-by-district; there is no single citywide school number.

health.heading: What this means for you
body: These are community-health indicators for the Burton area, such as chronic conditions and preventive care. They show where residents face the biggest health challenges, which helps the city, county, and providers aim clinics, screenings, and programs where they will do the most good. They describe the community overall, not any one person.

water.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows the quality and testing of Burton's drinking water. The city is required to test regularly and publish the results; meeting the standards means the water coming from your tap is safe to drink. It also reflects the water system your usage bills maintain, the same system behind most of the city's debt (see Financial Health).

environment.heading: What this means for you
body: These figures cover local environmental conditions such as air quality. They affect day-to-day health, especially for children, older adults, and people with breathing conditions. Tracking them over time shows whether conditions are improving and how the area compares with the region.

parks.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows the parks and green space within reach of Burton residents and who maintains each one. Parks are where families gather, kids play, and neighbors connect, and nearby green space supports both health and home values. It's a quick picture of the recreation available, whether a park is run by the city, the county, or a neighborhood.

broadband.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows how well Burton is covered by high-speed internet. Reliable broadband is now essential for school, working from home, telehealth, and running a business. Gaps point to where residents may struggle to get online, and where providers or grant dollars should focus next.

bridges.heading: What this means for you
body: This rates the condition of the bridges residents drive over every day. Bridges in poor shape signal where costly repairs are coming and where weight limits or closures could disrupt your commute. Keeping them in fair-or-better condition is far cheaper than waiting for them to fail.

roads.heading: What this means for you
body: This rates Burton's roads using the same PASER scale the road crews use. It explains why some streets are smooth and others rough, where repaving is most needed, and how Burton compares with the county. Road funding is limited (much of it is state gas-tax money, see City Finances), so condition reflects hard choices about where the dollars go.

roadsafety.heading: What this means for you
body: This summarizes years of reported crashes to show where and how they happen in Burton. It flags the intersections and crash types worth extra caution and helps the city and county target safety fixes like signals and turn lanes. It is historical: a multi-year pattern, not today's live conditions.

trails.heading: What this means for you
body: This shows the trails and pathways for walking and biking in Burton, both built and planned. Safe places to walk and ride support health, give kids and non-drivers a way to get around, and connect neighborhoods to parks and schools. The planned segments show where the network is headed next.

publicsafety.heading: What this means for you
body: The Burton Fire Department responds to far more than fires. Most calls are rescue and medical emergencies, hazardous conditions, and service calls. This shows how often the department responds and how quickly, so you can see the workload behind the fire millage on your tax bill and how prepared the city is when you call for help.
